title: Western Australia symmetrical pylon
description: In Western Australia, symmetrical pylons are mainly found around Perth and often carry two ground cables.

title: Western Australia asymmetrical pylon
description: Asymmetrical pylons in Western Australia often have a top that leans towards the half crossarm, and a rather thin cage. Seen in the south-west and in the Pilbara.

title: Western Australia delta pylon
description: Delta pylons in Western Australia only exist south of Perth. Their ground cables are attached to the sides of the peaks instead of the very top.

title: Western Australia barrel pylon
description: The few barrel pylons of Western Australia are mostly around Perth. They usually have two long peaks carrying the two ground cables.

title: South Australia asymmetrical pylon
description: Asymmetrical pylons are mainly found in the east of South Australia. Their peaks lean towards the half crossarm, but are thicker and longer than elsewhere in Australia.

title: South Australia symmetrical pylon
description: South Australian symmetrical pylons mostly have very long cages that are already wide below the lowest crossarm, and almost always two ground cables.

title: South Australia triangle pylon
description: Triangle pylons here often have a leaning peak integrated into the top crossarm, a combination only found in South Australia, in the Mid North.

title: Adelaide delta pylon
description: Delta pylons in South Australia are only found around Adelaide. The top hole just below the cage is square, whereas most Australian pylons have a triangular one.

title: Northern Territory pylons
description: The Northern Territory only has pylons around Darwin and along Highway 1 (the Stuart Highway) towards Katherine. They are rarely visible from the road, but seeing one narrows the location down to that corridor.

title: Queensland symmetrical pylon
description: Queensland has many symmetrical pylons along the coast from Cairns to Brisbane; their cage is relatively thin.

title: Queensland delta pylon
description: Delta pylons in Queensland have a kink in the crossbar, similar to Italian ones, which is unique within Australia. They are mostly found along the south-east coast.

title: Queensland triangle pylon
description: Triangle pylons are rare in Queensland. They have a thin cage and a peak that does not lean to the side. Seen around Townsville and the Atherton Tableland.

title: New South Wales delta pylon
description: Delta pylons in New South Wales have an elongated hole and a particularly steep V, unique within Australia.

title: New South Wales H-frame pylon
description: H-frame pylons are rather rare in Australia; many of them are in New South Wales.

title: New South Wales symmetrical pylon
description: Symmetrical pylons in New South Wales often have a very wide cage, with crossarms frequently rounded outwards, a design unique within Oceania. Mostly around Sydney, the Hunter and Canberra.

title: New South Wales asymmetrical pylon
description: As in Western Australia, the peak leans towards the half crossarm, but it is a bit longer: three sections in the peak instead of two. Seen around Broken Hill and in the Riverina.

title: Victoria triangle pylon
description: Triangle pylons in Victoria are often thin, like in Queensland, and have a peak; some have a small extension on the peak or a double peak. Mostly in western and central Victoria.

title: Victoria symmetrical pylon
description: Victoria has many symmetrical pylons with a thin cage and dense mesh. The peak can be long, like in New Zealand, or normal; rarely a kind of plate sits on the peak.

title: Victoria delta pylon
description: Victorian delta pylons often have particularly long crossarms extending outwards, and the cables are often hung from two insulators in a V shape, unique within Australia. Mostly around Melbourne and in the north-east.

title: Tasmania symmetrical pylon
description: Tasmanian symmetrical pylons typically have crossarms that start at the tower body. Tops range from none to two peaks; rarely, an ultra-long peak like in New Zealand.

title: Tasmania delta pylon
description: Tasmanian delta pylons mostly have an upside-down kite-shaped square in their tower body, unique to Tasmania. Mostly in the centre and the west.

title: Tasmania barrel pylon
description: Tasmania has a single stretch of barrel pylons, from central Tasmania to Hobart. They are particularly large and visible from a distance.
